tips.title: Thinning Vallejo Model Air for Airbrushing
tips.text: Vallejo Model Air is slightly thicker than Tamiya acrylics. Thinner it at a 1:1 ratio with Tamiya Plastic Cement (436) or Vallejo Airbrush Thinner (71.261) for optimal flow. Add 1-2 drops of Vallejo Flow Improver (71.234) per 10 drops of thinned paint to enhance atomization. Test on a white plastic spoon — if it flows smoothly without clogging, the ratio is correct. Use a 0.2mm nozzle and spray at 1.2-1.5 bar pressure. Avoid over-thinning to prevent color loss and muddiness.

tips.title: Base Coat with Vallejo Model Color
tips.text: Apply a base coat of Vallejo Model Color using a 1:1 mix with Tamiya Plastic Cement. Use a 1.5mm brush for even coverage. For fast drying, use a small brush and apply thin layers. Allow 15 minutes between coats. Avoid thick layers to prevent cracking. After base coat, apply a clear coat of Tamiya Clear Enamel (433) to seal and enhance color vibrancy. This prevents oxidation and ensures a smooth surface for weathering.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking with Clear Prop Models Film
tips.text: Use Clear Prop Models camouflage film for precise masking. Cut the film using a scalpel blade and apply it with a Tamiya plastic cement brush. Ensure the film is tightly adhered to the surface. For intricate patterns, use a small flat brush to apply thin layers of paint. Remove the film immediately after the paint dries to avoid sticking. This method ensures sharp edges and clean lines, ideal for military aircraft or armor.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes for Weathering
tips.text: AK Interactive washes are ideal for detailed weathering. Dilute them at a 1:3 ratio with Tamiya Plastic Cement. Apply using a felt brush or sponge for even coverage. For best results, use a 0.3mm brush and work in thin layers. Allow 5-10 minutes drying time between layers. This technique enhances the depth and realism of your model's surface, especially on metal or fabric areas.

tips.title: Chipping with Sponge Technique for Realism
tips.text: Use a sponge applicator with Tamiya Clear Enamel (433) for chipping effects. Apply the enamel in light strokes, focusing on areas where wear is likely. Use a dry sponge to create a weathered texture. For added realism, mix in a small amount of Alclad II Weathering Color (808) for a muted chipped effect. Work in thin layers and allow drying time between passes. This method mimics natural wear without the need for complex tools.
